key_insight: GenEHR is a generative EHR model that learns patient health trajectories, including irregular visit timing, to better forecast who is at elevated risk of a first cancer diagnosis within five years.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help prioritize patients for risk-based cancer screening, especially for aggressive cancers such as pancreatic and ovarian cancer.
method: Trained autoregressively on longitudinal electronic health records from millions of patients.
Represents irregular time intervals between visits when predicting future clinical events.
Uses parameter-efficient supervised adaptation to specialize the general patient model for pan-cancer risk stratification.
evidence_signal: In five large EHR cohorts, supervised adaptation substantially improved prediction of first cancer diagnosis within a five-year horizon.
watch_item: The findings are retrospective, so prospective validation is still needed before clinical decision-support use.
paper_title: Identifying cohorts at elevated risk of cancers using generative modeling of patient health states
